methods.name: Guided Flows for Generative Modeling and Decision Making (CFG for flow matching)
methods.mechanism: Extends classifier-free guidance to flow matching: the sampled velocity is v_guided = v_uncond + w(v_cond - v_uncond), justified by the fact that for affine Gaussian paths the marginal velocity is an affine function of the score, so score-space guidance carries over to velocity space. First to use FM plan generation in offline RL, with 10x speedup over diffusion planners at comparable return.
methods.when_it_wins: Wins when a conditional signal was (or can be) trained in; nearly free at inference (one extra forward pass or none with amortization). Fails for post-hoc constraints never seen in training, and over-guiding causes off-manifold drift exactly like CFG in diffusion.
methods.relevance_to_us: Establishes the velocity<->score dictionary we need for everything else: pi0.5's velocity field gives us a score estimate for free (for Gaussian source), which unlocks SMC drift correction and energy guidance. Not directly usable for safety (no safety conditioning trained into pi0.5), but the affine-path assumption holds for pi0.5's linear interpolant, so all diffusion-guidance theory ports over.

methods.name: On the Guidance of Flow Matching (general FM guidance theory)
methods.venue_year: arXiv Feb 2025 (v3 May 2025), Feng, Yu, Deng, Hu, Wu
methods.mechanism: First general framework for energy-guided flow matching, showing FM guidance is strictly more general than diffusion guidance (arbitrary source distributions and paths, not just Gaussian). Derives (a) a training-free asymptotically exact guidance via Monte Carlo estimation of the energy-tilted posterior velocity, (b) training losses for learned guidance networks, and (c) two classes of approximate gradient guidance that recover classical methods (gradient on the interpolant x_t, gradient on the one-step x1-prediction) as special cases, with theory on when each approximation is valid.
methods.when_it_wins: The exact MC guidance wins when the energy is cheap to evaluate and moderate accuracy per step suffices; gradient-on-x1-prediction wins when the energy is smooth and differentiable; gradient-on-x_t is worst near t=0 where the interpolant is far from the data manifold. All degrade for stiff/discontinuous energies (which hard barriers are).
methods.relevance_to_us: This is the theoretical backbone for a 'soft pre-shaping' stage: define energy U = sum of ReLU(-(B_j - (1-gamma)B_{j-1})) over our ECBF chain evaluated on the one-step Euler x1-prediction, and add -eta_t * grad U to the velocity in steps 1-6 BEFORE our hard sweep. Their theory says use x1-prediction gradients (not raw x_t gradients) for a 10-step Euler solver, and warns our barrier energy should be softened (squared hinge) to avoid the stiff-energy failure mode.

methods.name: FK-Steering: A General Framework for Inference-time Scaling and Steering of Diffusion Models
methods.mechanism: Runs K interacting particles through denoising and resamples them at intermediate steps via multinomial selection with Feynman-Kac potentials: difference exp(lambda(r_t - r_{t+1})), max exp(lambda max_s r_s), or sum potentials, where intermediate rewards r are computed on the expected-x0 (Tweedie) prediction. Any potential satisfying the FK constraint yields asymptotically exact samples from the reward-tilted distribution; works with non-differentiable rewards.
methods.when_it_wins: Beats best-of-N at equal K (k=4 FK > k=4 BoN on prompt fidelity; FK-steered 0.8B model beats a fine-tuned 2.6B model) because it reallocates compute mid-trajectory instead of only filtering at the end. Only k=2-8 particles needed. Loses value when the reward is uninformative at intermediate steps or when resampling collapses diversity too early (mitigated by interval resampling — score only at a few timesteps).
methods.relevance_to_us: Directly upgrades our planned P4 best-of-K: best-of-K with terminal acceptance is degenerate FK (resample once at t=1). At the SAME batch size, add 2-3 mid-trajectory resampling points with potential = lexicographic (ECBF-chain feasibility of the x1-Euler-prediction, then margin+progress), non-differentiability is fine. Expected benefit: kill infeasible seeds early and reallocate NFEs to promising ones, raising the chance the executed 5-step prefix passes the terminal test — direct CAR gain at fixed compute.

methods.name: Twisted Diffusion Sampler (TDS) / Filtering Posterior Sampling (FPS) lineage
methods.venue_year: NeurIPS 2023 / ICLR 2024, with 2025-26 successors (Trust-Region Iterative Twisted SMC arXiv 2605.25123, Diffusion Tree Sampling 2506.20701)
methods.mechanism: Casts conditional sampling as SMC over the denoising chain with twisted proposals: each transition kernel is tilted by an approximate value function (twist) p(y|x0_hat(x_t)), and importance weights correct the twist approximation so the particle system is asymptotically exact for the true posterior. FPS shows the same problem is Bayesian filtering; successors iterate to improve twists (trust-region updates around the current proposal) or organize particles in a tree to reuse partial trajectories.
methods.when_it_wins: Wins over pure gradient guidance when the posterior is multimodal or the likelihood is stiff — weights + resampling can jump between basins that gradient flows cannot cross. Costs K parallel model evals; degenerates when twists are poor at high noise (weight variance) or K is small relative to mode count.
methods.relevance_to_us: The twist-quality lesson matters for us: our ECBF margin evaluated on x1-predictions IS a twist, and it is unreliable at early steps (x1-prediction of a flow at t~0 is nearly the chunk mean). So weight/resample only from mid-trajectory onward (harmonic/late schedules below), and treat early-step margins as advisory only. Trust-region iteration is overkill for 10 steps; single-pass twisted resampling is the right operating point.

methods.name: Feynman-Kac-Flow: Inference Steering of Conditional Flow Matching to an Energy-Tilted Posterior
methods.mechanism: First derivation of FK/SMC steering for deterministic CFM: converts the ODE to a family of SDEs with the same marginals by injecting isotropic noise sigma(t) and correcting the drift using the score, which for Gaussian-source CFM is expressed directly from the velocity field (no score net needed): drift = v_t + (sigma^2/2) * s_t(v_t, x_t). Particles are weighted with a difference potential exp(-lambda(U(y_t)-U(y_{t-1}))) where y_t is the one-step Euler x1-prediction, resampled multinomially, with a 'harmonic sum' schedule that down-weights early resampling steps where x1-predictions are inaccurate.
methods.when_it_wins: On high-dimensional energy-tilted targets, FK-Flow isolates the correct mode with few particles where gradient guidance and importance sampling suffer the curse of dimensionality; solved reaction-transition-state chirality that guidance could not. Fails when potentials are discontinuous indicators and particle count < mode count — a soft margin potential is essential.
methods.relevance_to_us: This is the exact recipe to make our frozen pi0.5 ODE SMC-able: the drift-corrected noise injection formula plus velocity-derived score means no retraining and no auxiliary model. Two lessons transfer verbatim: (1) use a SOFT margin potential (our signed ECBF margin), never the 0/1 feasibility indicator; (2) adopt their harmonic early-step down-weighting — it is the SMC analogue of our '+4mm/step margin inflation' intuition (trust late, not early).

methods.name: BayesFP: Posterior Estimation for Flow-Based Policies via Feynman-Kac Sampling
methods.mechanism: Frames constrained action generation for flow/diffusion policies as Bayesian posterior sampling: the demonstration distribution is the prior, an inference-time cost-derived likelihood (e.g., obstacle clearance) tilts it, and a Feynman-Kac corrector particle system samples the posterior over the flow integration without retraining. Unifies diffusion and flow policies in one retraining-free sampler.
methods.when_it_wins: Wins for constraints introduced at inference time (non-convex obstacle avoidance added post-training) while preserving demonstration fidelity — exactly the regime where naive projection distorts actions and fine-tuning is impossible. Evaluated on Diffusion Policy, GR00T-N1.6, and pi0.5, improving over base pi0.5 zero-shot. As a soft/probabilistic method it gives no per-sample hard guarantee.
methods.relevance_to_us: Closest existing system to our stack — FK sampling on pi0.5 itself with inference-time obstacle costs. It validates that particle steering works at pi0.5 scale and step counts. Our differentiator vs BayesFP should be the combination: their FK posterior tilt for TSR-preserving soft steering + our hard ECBF sweep for the guarantee they lack. Worth benchmarking against and citing as the soft-only ablation point.

methods.name: GLASS Flows: Transition Sampling for Alignment of Flow and Diffusion Models
methods.mechanism: Enables stochastic Markov transitions p(x_t'|x_t) in a pretrained flow model without SDE discretization error: a sufficient-statistic compression of (x_t, x_t') yields an 'inner' flow matching model retrievable from the pretrained denoiser with one forward pass, so branching/resampling moves are simulated with ODE-quality accuracy. Plugged into FK steering on FLUX: CLIP reward 34.9 -> 39.8 without reward hacking, beating best-of-N.
methods.when_it_wins: Wins when SMC/tree search needs high-quality stochastic branching but the few-step SDE conversion is too noisy (exactly the 10-step regime, where Euler-Maruyama error is large). Costs extra inner-flow integration per branch, so it loses on raw wall-clock vs simple noise injection when step counts are high.
methods.relevance_to_us: If we adopt FK resampling on pi0.5's 10-step Euler chain and find that naive sigma(t) noise injection (FK-Flow style) degrades action quality — a real risk at 10 steps — GLASS is the fix: accurate branching transitions without shrinking step size. Treat as the second-line tool; try drift-corrected noise injection first since it is one line of code.

methods.name: Psi-Sampler: Initial Particle Sampling for SMC-Based Inference-Time Reward Alignment
methods.mechanism: Instead of drawing SMC initial particles from the Gaussian prior, runs preconditioned Crank-Nicolson Langevin (pCNL) MCMC in the NOISE space, targeting the reward-aware posterior pulled back to t=1 via the model's x1-prediction: x' = rho*x + sqrt(1-rho^2)(z + (sqrt(eps)/2) grad r(x0|1)/alpha). pCN preconditioning keeps acceptance rates dimension-robust (works in 65k-dim latents where MALA collapses).
methods.when_it_wins: Wins when the reward/constraint signal vanishes late in sampling (small diffusion coefficient) so seed choice dominates outcome, and when modes are connected at t=1 but disconnected later. Adds MCMC burn-in cost before generation; needs a differentiable reward through the x1-prediction.
methods.relevance_to_us: Key upgrade to P4's iid best-of-K seeds: for a DETERMINISTIC 10-step Euler map, the seed fully determines the chunk, so searching seed space intelligently beats blind sampling. Our ECBF margin on the one-step x1-prediction is differentiable through pi0.5 in the translational dims — a few pCNL steps could concentrate the K seeds on the feasible-and-progressing set, multiplying effective K without more rollout batch. Expected: better feasible-seed hit rate on L1 (obstacle-near-target) where the feasible set is thin.

methods.name: Inference-Time Scaling for Diffusion Models beyond Denoising Steps (noise-space search)
methods.mechanism: Formulates inference-time scaling as search over sampling noises with two axes: the verifier providing feedback and the search algorithm (random/best-of-N, zero-order local search around promising seeds, and search-over-paths which branches at intermediate steps and prunes with the verifier). Shows monotone quality gains with search compute, far beyond what more denoising steps give.
methods.when_it_wins: Wins when a reliable verifier exists; the central failure mode is verifier hacking — a mis-aligned verifier makes search actively harmful (over-optimized artifacts). Zero-order search wins over random when good seeds cluster; search-over-paths wins when intermediate states are informative.
methods.relevance_to_us: Blueprint for P4. Our verifier is unusually trustworthy (GT-state ECBF margins — no hacking risk on the safety axis; progress term is the hackable part, so keep it lexicographically second). Zero-order refinement applies directly: after a seed passes, perturb it locally to climb margin+progress instead of drawing fresh seeds. Search-over-paths = FK resampling (above). Their scaling curves justify reporting a CAR/TSR-vs-K compute curve as a paper figure.

methods.name: RoboMonkey / VLA verifier line (test-time sampling + verification for VLAs)
methods.mechanism: Samples N action candidates from a VLA, scores them with a learned action-verifier (VLM fine-tuned to rank actions given the observation) or task-progress verifier, and executes the argmax; verifier-free variants score by agreement/consistency across samples. Findings: scaling verification beats scaling policy learning; gains grow with sampling temperature/diversity.
methods.when_it_wins: Wins when policy failure is 'right distribution, wrong sample' — multimodal outputs where some modes fail. Loses when all modes are unsafe (verifier can only select, not repair) and adds a verifier-training burden; consistency scoring is weak on safety-critical tail events.
methods.relevance_to_us: We already have RoboMonkey/TACO/BOKBO in our notes; the new lesson from this line is the SELECTION-vs-REPAIR complementarity: selection preserves TSR (picks an on-manifold sample) while our projection guarantees CAR (repairs when no sample is feasible). Lexicographic P4 is exactly right; add the diversity knob — inject seed diversity (temperature on source noise) or the selection has nothing to choose among, especially with only 10 deterministic steps.

methods.name: SafeDiffuser: time-varying relaxed CBF invariance in denoising (local-trap fix)
methods.mechanism: Embeds finite-time CBF invariance as a QP on each denoising update; the Relaxed/Time-Varying-Safe variants add a slack variable whose penalty weight is time-varying — near-free relaxation early in denoising, decaying to zero so the constraint becomes exactly hard only at the end. This prevents 'local traps' where hard constraints at every noisy iterate freeze the sample against the barrier boundary in a spurious local minimum.
methods.when_it_wins: Wins whenever hard per-step enforcement conflicts with the prior's transport early in denoising (constraint surfaces are meaningless for noisy iterates); the time-varying schedule provably retains the terminal guarantee while restoring plasticity. Failure mode: slack scheduling adds hyperparameters, and per-step QPs are slow (our jittable sweep already solves that part).
methods.relevance_to_us: Already in our notes, but the SCHEDULE is the under-exploited part: we currently apply the full-strength hard sweep after EVERY Euler step with fixed gamma=0.9. Port their idea as a denoising-time-dependent gamma_k or slack: steps 1-5 enforce a relaxed chain (larger allowed decay, or penalty-weighted repair), steps 6-10 tighten to the current hard sweep. This directly targets our L1-fat TSR collapse (58.5) — early hard repairs near the target corridor are what fight task progress.

methods.name: Uehara et al.: Inference-Time Alignment with Reward-Guided Generation — Tutorial and Review (SOC view)
methods.mechanism: Unifies inference-time steering as approximating the SOFT-OPTIMAL denoising policy of an entropy-regularized stochastic optimal control problem: the exact optimum tilts each transition by the value function V_t(x) = log E[exp(r(x0))|x_t], and every method family is an approximation of V — classifier guidance (gradient of V), SVDD/value-based resampling (pointwise V), SMC (importance-corrected V), best-of-N (V only at t=0/terminal), tree search (deeper V estimates).
methods.when_it_wins: As a lens: gradient methods win with smooth rewards and accurate x0-predictions; sampling/resampling methods win with non-differentiable or stiff rewards; combining both (gradient proposal + FK correction weights) dominates either alone. The value function estimated via x0-prediction is systematically biased early in denoising for all families.
methods.relevance_to_us: Gives us the unifying vocabulary for the paper and a concrete architecture: our ECBF margin chain defines a natural value function V(x_t) = margin of the x1-prediction rollout; use grad V as the soft proposal (pre-shaping), FK weights as correction, hard sweep as terminal enforcement. Also predicts our P4 terminal test is the weakest V estimator (terminal-only) — mid-trajectory V evaluations are near-free since we already run the ECBF rollout machinery per step.

methods.name: Adaptive Diffusion Guidance via Stochastic Optimal Control (state/time-dependent guidance weight)
methods.mechanism: Treats the guidance STRENGTH w as a control variable and solves max E[log p(c|Y_T)] - lambda*KL(guided||unguided) via the HJB equation, yielding a closed-form optimal schedule w*_t(x) = [grad G_t . grad V_t + ||grad G_t||^2] / (lambda ||grad G_t||^2) that depends on both state and time; trained via Girsanov importance reweighting. Proves guidance increases classifier confidence while STAYING inside the conditional data support.
methods.when_it_wins: Adaptive schedules crush constant weights on synthetic tasks (reward 8.1 vs 5.2, KL 0.77 vs 1.66) where score estimates are exact; the authors could NOT get significant real-image gains because learned score error dominates. So it wins when the 'score' is accurate — or when the reward gradient is exact.
methods.relevance_to_us: Their failure condition does not apply to us: our 'reward' (ECBF margin under GT obstacle state) is exact, not learned. The practical takeaway is a principled correction-strength schedule: scale the soft pre-shaping step size by violation magnitude of the x1-prediction normalized by its gradient norm (their w* structure), i.e., push hard only when-and-where the predicted chunk actually violates. This replaces a hand-tuned constant eta and is the SOC-blessed version of 'corridor exemption' (P3): near the sanctioned approach, grad G of the safety classifier shrinks, automatically relaxing the correction.

methods.name: VGG-Flow: Value Gradient Guidance for Flow Matching Alignment
methods.mechanism: Shows the optimal residual velocity for reward-aligning a flow model equals the value-function gradient (HJB matching): v_aligned = v_theta + beta*g_phi(x,t), where g_phi is parameterized as -eta_t * grad r(x1_hat) (one-step Euler prediction, stop-gradient) plus a small learned correction net trained by an HJB consistency loss. The reward-gradient term alone is a training-free approximation.
methods.when_it_wins: Preserves diversity and prior fidelity far better than direct reward optimization (FID 375 vs 1338-1518 for ReFL/DRaFT at comparable reward) because the value-gradient structure is KL-regularized by construction. The pure training-free term wins when one-step x1-predictions are decent; the learned correction matters when they are not (early t).
methods.relevance_to_us: Validates the exact form our soft pre-shaping stage should take on pi0.5: add -eta_t * grad_x [ECBF-margin-hinge(x1_hat(x_t))] to the velocity, with eta_t ramping over flow time. Their finding that this preserves prior fidelity is the mechanism by which we expect to RECOVER TSR relative to hard-projection-only (which currently costs us up to 13 TSR points on L1-fat). No training needed if we skip the correction net.

methods.name: Applying Guidance in a Limited Interval (guidance schedules over denoising time)
methods.mechanism: Replaces constant guidance weight with a piecewise schedule active only on a middle interval of noise levels (e.g., sigma in [17,22] of [0,80]): guidance at high noise drastically drifts trajectories (the conditional/unconditional score gap is large and misaligned with the data manifold, causing mode drops), while at low noise the two scores coincide so guidance is wasted compute. ImageNet-512 FID 1.81 -> 1.40 purely from scheduling.
methods.when_it_wins: Wins essentially always over constant-weight guidance for distribution-level fidelity; interval endpoints need per-model tuning. Note the finding is about DISTRIBUTION quality of conditioning-type guidance — for hard constraint satisfaction the late phase cannot be skipped, it must transition from guidance to enforcement.
methods.relevance_to_us: Merged with SafeDiffuser's schedule, this fixes our correction timing: early steps (1-3 of 10) should receive NEITHER strong soft gradients NOR full hard projection (both fight the prior; x1-predictions are unreliable anyway); middle steps (3-7) get soft value-gradient pre-shaping; late steps (7-10) get the hard ECBF sweep. Our current uniform-over-steps hard repair is precisely the 'constant weight' anti-pattern this paper kills.

methods.name: Fisher-Preserving Guidance: training-free manifold constraints for safe diffusion control
methods.mechanism: Measures manifold drift as change in Fisher information (sensitivity of the denoiser output to conditioning, via input-output Jacobian) and projects each guidance/correction update onto the Fisher isosurface: decompose the safety-guidance gradient into components parallel/orthogonal to the Fisher normal g_t and keep only the component with g_t^T Delta_t = 0. Low-rank OPS factorization makes it one backward pass per step; Truncated FDS accumulates drift only over the last 4-6 steps.
methods.when_it_wins: Wins when external safety gradients (TSDF obstacle costs) push samples into low-confidence off-manifold regions: Maze2D collisions 0.071 -> 0.016 WITH better path quality; PushT 0.91 -> 0.94 on frozen Diffusion Policy weights; real-robot navigation 28/30 vs 19/30. Adds Jacobian cost; the projection can slow constraint satisfaction when the feasible direction is mostly off-manifold.
methods.relevance_to_us: The most direct manifold-drift-control tool for our repair sweep: our in-order per-waypoint clamp can shear the chunk off pi0.5's action manifold (plausibly the source of L1 TSR loss — repaired chunks the policy 'would never produce'). Two adoptable ideas: (1) project the soft pre-shaping gradient tangent to the model's sensitivity structure; (2) cheaper proxy — after each hard repair, take one extra denoiser evaluation on the repaired chunk so the base velocity field re-attracts it to the manifold (the 'recurrence' trick, see TFG). Measure drift via their truncated-late-steps recipe.

methods.name: TFG: Unified Training-Free Guidance (design-space + recurrence)
methods.mechanism: Unifies training-free guidance into an algorithm design space with four knobs: mean guidance (gradient on x0-prediction), variance guidance (second-order/gradient on x_t), implicit dynamics (Gaussian-smoothed predictor), and RECURRENCE — after applying guidance at step t, re-noise the sample back to t and re-denoise, iterating so the base model repeatedly projects the guided sample back toward the data manifold. Benchmarked over 7 models/16 tasks; +8.5% average over prior training-free methods.
methods.when_it_wins: Recurrence is the single most robust knob when guidance is strong or the target is far from the prior (it trades compute for manifold consistency); mean+variance combo wins on smooth predictors. Fails on extremely stiff objectives without smoothing (implicit dynamics fixes some of this).
methods.relevance_to_us: Recurrence is the cheapest manifold-drift fix for our hard projection: after the ECBF sweep repairs the intermediate chunk at step k, perturb back with matched noise and take one extra pi0.5 velocity step before continuing. At 10 steps, adding recurrence on 2-3 middle steps costs 20-30% NFEs and should reclaim TSR by letting the policy 'digest' our repairs. The Gaussian-smoothed-predictor idea also suggests smoothing our hinge margin for the soft stage.

methods.name: Mirror / Reflected / Gauge / Chance-Constrained Flow Matching (constrained-domain flow family)
methods.id_or_url: https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.08929 (Mirror FM heavy-tailed); Reflected FM ICML 2024; https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.25157 (chance-constrained FM)
methods.mechanism: Three ways to build constraints INTO the flow rather than correcting after: reflected flows bounce trajectories off boundary normals; mirror flows learn the flow in the image of a mirror map of a convex domain so primal samples are feasible by construction (100% feasibility, better FID than mirror diffusion at less training time); gauge/chance-constrained variants learn constraint-aware vector fields with probabilistic feasibility levels. All require the constraint set to be known at TRAINING time and (for mirror) convex.
methods.when_it_wins: Wins when constraints are fixed, convex(ish), and known before training — zero inference overhead and exact feasibility. Loses completely for our setting: scene-dependent, non-convex unions of obstacle sets decided at inference from perception.
methods.relevance_to_us: Mostly a negative result that sharpens our positioning: constraint-embedding (PolyFlow included) cannot handle per-episode semantic constraint sets, which is our whole premise. One salvageable idea: a mirror-like smooth reparameterization AROUND the target corridor (P3) — define the corridor once per episode and do the late-step hard sweep in corridor-adapted coordinates so repairs slide along the corridor instead of blocking approach.

methods.name: ITPS: Inference-Time Policy Steering through Human Interactions (alignment-vs-shift tradeoff)
methods.venue_year: arXiv Nov 2024 / ICRA 2025 (Wang et al., MIT)
methods.mechanism: Compares six ways to inject steering objectives into diffusion/flow policy sampling (output perturbation, biased initialization, gradient guidance at various stages, stochastic sampling with objective-weighted selection) and measures BOTH objective alignment and distribution shift. Finding: stochastic-sampling-based selection achieves the best alignment-per-unit-shift; naive gradient guidance and output-space perturbation cause the most constraint violations via distribution shift.
methods.when_it_wins: Sample-then-select wins when the base policy has enough multimodal coverage that some sample already aligns; gradient guidance wins when no sample does but shifts distribution. The tradeoff frontier, not any single method, is the contribution.
methods.relevance_to_us: Already in our notes but its ranking now slots into the unified picture: their 'stochastic sampling' = our P4 best-of-K (least shift), their 'guidance' = our soft pre-shaping (moderate shift), our hard projection = their 'output perturbation' (most shift). Order interventions by shift-cost: select first (seeds), guide second (mid-steps), project last (late steps + executed prefix) — only escalating when the cheaper level fails to produce feasibility.

key_insights:
Six cross-cutting lessons emerge for our DCBF-in-denoising pi0.5 system.

(1) Schedules are the highest-leverage free lunch. Every mature line converges on the same asymmetry: corrections at early denoising time are unreliable (x1-predictions near t=0 are close to the chunk mean; constraint surfaces are meaningless for noisy iterates) and actively harmful to fidelity (guidance-interval NeurIPS'24: constant weight is the anti-pattern; SafeDiffuser: early hard constraints cause local traps; FK-Flow: harmonic down-weighting of early resampling). Late steps are where hard enforcement is both meaningful and cheap. Our uniform per-step hard sweep with fixed gamma is the identified anti-pattern — a denoising-time schedule (steps 1-3 untouched, 3-7 soft value-gradient pre-shaping on the x1-Euler prediction, 7-10 hard ECBF sweep, plus terminal test on the executed prefix) is the single most evidence-backed change, directly targeting our L1-fat TSR collapse.

(2) Escalation ordering by distribution shift. ITPS quantifies it and the SOC view (Uehara) explains it: select (seeds) < guide (velocity tilt) < project (output clamp) in shift cost. Escalate only on infeasibility.

(3) Stability of soft guidance requires x1-prediction gradients, softened hinges, and adaptive strength. Gradient guidance on raw x_t fails at low t (Feng et al.); stiff/indicator potentials break both gradients and particles (FK-Flow); the SOC-optimal strength w*(x,t) scales with actual violation and is available in closed form — and unlike image domains, our reward (GT-state ECBF margin) is exact, so adaptive schedules should realize their synthetic-benchmark gains.

(4) Particle methods are the right upgrade path for P4. Best-of-K with terminal acceptance is degenerate FK; at fixed batch, mid-trajectory resampling with margin-based potentials dominates (FK-Steering, k=2-8 suffices). Deterministic flows need stochasticity: drift-corrected noise injection using the velocity-derived score (FK-Flow, one line of code) or GLASS transitions if 10-step SDE error bites. BayesFP already demonstrates this on pi0.5 — our edge must be the hard-guarantee layer they lack. Seed search should be informed, not iid: pCNL in noise space (Psi-Sampler) or zero-order refinement around feasible seeds (Ma et al.), with the verifier-alignment caveat neutralized by keeping safety lexicographically first.

(5) Manifold drift is the mechanism behind projection's TSR cost, and it is controllable: Fisher-isosurface projection of corrections (FPG: fewer collisions AND better task scores), or the cheaper recurrence trick (TFG: re-noise/re-denoise after repair so the frozen policy re-attracts the chunk).

(6) Guarantees don't come from soft methods — SMC is exact only in distribution, guidance not at all. The defensible architecture is soft steering for TSR + late hard projection and executed-prefix enforcement (SafeFlowMatcher-style) for CAR. Nobody yet combines FK particle steering, scheduled soft pre-shaping, and a hard discrete-ECBF sweep on a frozen VLA — that composition is our paper.
